sections.label: Definition of false statement
sections.summary: The Bill defines a statement as false if it is false or misleading, wholly or partly, alone or in context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, a statement is false if it is false or misleading, whether wholly or in part, and whether on its own or in the context in which it appears.

sections.label: WP objects to Minister arbiter
sections.summary: The WP objects to the Minister being an arbiter and wants the Courts to be the sole arbiter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The WP objects to the Minister being an arbiter under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We think that the Minister in question should apply to the Courts for an order under this Bill and let the Courts be the sole arbiter.

sections.label: POFMA and POHA procedures differ
sections.summary: The procedure under POFMA differs from POHA, where the Court is truly the one and only arbiter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Significantly, the procedure under POFMA is different from the procedure in POHA where the Court there is truly the one and only arbiter.

sections.label: Courts should decide POFMA applications
sections.summary: The speaker says Courts should have exclusive rights to decide POFMA applications at first instance, covering all areas and issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my view, the Courts should be given the exclusive rights to decide on any application under POFMA at first instance and the Courts' jurisdiction should extend to all areas and issues under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, I think the same Court should handle and decide both POHA and POFMA applications.

sections.label: No proof needed for Directions
sections.summary: In POFMA, the aggrieved party need not prove to any authority when first deciding on a Direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In POFMA, the aggrieved party, in this case a Minister or the Government, does not have to prove to any authority or adjudicator when it first decides on a Direction under the Bill, such as a Correction Direction or a stop communication Direction.

sections.label: Burden of proof in appeals
sections.summary: The burden of proof in an appeal under clause 17 or 29 appears to be on the person subject to the Directions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The burden of proof in an appeal under clause 17 or 29 of POFMA appears to be on the person who is the subject of a Minister's Directions under POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Surely, the Minister and the Government, as the aggrieved party, must always bear the burden of proof for any Direction or order under POFMA.

sections.label: Chilling effect fear
sections.summary: The speaker fears the Bill will create a chilling effect for journalists, interest groups, academics and average Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Like many Singaporeans, I fear that the Bill, if passed, will create a chilling effect, whether for journalists, legitimate interest groups, academics or the average Singaporean.

sections.label: WP cannot support Bill
sections.summary: The speaker and WP colleagues cannot support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Along with my WP colleagues, I cannot support the Bill.

sections.label: Groups concerned about Bill
sections.summary: Academics, civil society groups, media, jurists, a UN rapporteur and ASEAN parliamentarians expressed concern about the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One hundred and twenty-four academics in Singapore and abroad, including 52 Singaporeans, signed a statement expressing concern that the Bill could adversely affect academic research on Singapore, especially in social sciences, where critical research contests established facts and narratives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Other parties expressing concern include 30 Singaporean civil society and arts community organisations, The Asia Internet Coalition, traditional and independent online media, the International Commission of Jurists, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Promotion and Protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression, and the ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will stand corrected, but I do not think these parties are enemies of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I do not think they are agents of the forces who propagate online falsehoods.

sections.label: Correction Directions as tools
sections.summary: The Bill creates tools such as Correction Directions to stop imminent harm while preserving online speech and promoting public education.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They spread virally, and when there is a threat of imminent harm to society, the Government has a duty to act immediately to stop the threat.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill will create novel and proportionate tools, such as Correction Directions, that preserve online speech and promote public education while minimising harm.

sections.label: Agreement on two-part test
sections.summary: The speaker accepts the two-part test for Executive action, including the falsehood definition and broad public interest definition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Before I explain our amendments further, I wish to first touch on points of agreement with the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We accept the two-part test for Executive action, including the definition of falsehood and the broad definition of the public interest.

sections.label: Institution-building amendments proposed
sections.summary: The amendments limit Executive discretion through the Principles of Act and an Independent Council Against Online Falsehoods, with public justification and expedited appeals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rather, we decided to do what is the best way we feel of limiting the discretion of the Executive was to ensure that we develop robust institutions within and without Government, to address online Falsehoods without fear or favour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These institution-building amendments have two major parts, namely, the Principles of Act, and the Independent Council Against Online Falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, our amendments require that any Directions issued are publicly justified and require that the appeals process is expedited.

sections.label: Principles of Act on speech
sections.summary: The Principles of Act state free critical speech is necessary for democracy, so the Act should be applied proportionately, with Corrections first and takedowns only when necessary, and research differences do not imply falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Principles of Act state that well-informed, free and critical speech is necessary for a well-functioning democracy, so the Act should be applied carefully to avoid chilling such speech.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It sets out that the Act should be used proportionately, so the least restrictive tools, such as Corrections, are used first, with the most restrictive, that is, takedowns used only when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also protects the role of research in society as research often contests established facts or ideas in order to advance knowledge by stating that differences in facts established by an authority and a researcher do not imply falsehood just by that difference alone.

sections.label: Third way for online falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker asks why not a third way of strengthening the Civil Service's capacity to implement the rules fairly, guided by the Principles, given practical difficulties with Courts deciding fast-moving online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we know there may be practical difficulties with having the Courts decide on fast-moving online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, why not a third way, why not strengthen the capacity of the Civil Service to implement these rules fairly, guided by the Principles?

sections.label: Review of Government misinformation actions
sections.summary: The speaker reviewed Government actions against misinformation from 2015 to 2019, documenting Factually posts and MOM and MSF Fact Checks, and established for each whether POFM would apply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way to answer this is to examine how the Government has already been addressing the problem of online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I conducted a review of Government actions against misinformation from 2015 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This review documented all posts on the Government's Factually website, as well as Fact Checks issued by MOM and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I first established for each Government action whether POFM would apply.

sections.label: Analysis of 170 misinformation cases
sections.summary: The speaker analysed 170 Government actions against online misinformation from 2015 to 2019, finding 110 involved no disputed facts and most would not have used the Act's powers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it mainly a dispute over facts or a dispute over conclusions drawn from facts that are not themselves contested?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I analysed 170 cases of Government action against online misinformation from 2015 to 2019; 110 cases involve no disputed facts, they are simply clarifications of policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Most Government actions on misinformation over the last few years would not have used any powers under the Act because it does not apply.

sections.label: Concern over declared falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about cases declared falsehoods by the Government's language although the dispute is actually over conclusions drawn from facts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: What I am concerned about are those cases which are declared to be falsehoods by the language the Government uses, although the dispute is actually over conclusions drawn from facts.

sections.label: Support for Bill with protections
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the Bill's principles and supports Second Reading but finds it difficult to support final passage unless satisfied the Bill contains strong protections against abuse by an unjust future government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I agree with the principles of the Bill, and I support the Second Reading of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: But I find it difficult to support final passage of this Bill unless I am satisfied the Bill contains strong protections against abuse by an unjust future government.

sections.label: Conscience vote request
sections.summary: The speaker calls the matter one of policy and conscience and hopes the Government will consider allowing a conscience vote for its Members.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: But for me, this is a matter of policy and of conscience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider allowing a conscience vote for its Members.

sections.label: Bill's two conjunctive conditions
sections.summary: The speaker understands from Minister Shanmugam that the Bill applies only on two conjunctive conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As I understand listening to Minister Shanmugam, this Bill applies only on two conjunctive conditions.

sections.label: Kidnapper rumours on social media
sections.summary: In March, videos on Facebook, Snapchat and others claimed kidnappers in vans abducted children for prostitution and illegal organ trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In March this year, videos circulating on Facebook, Snapchat and so on claimed that kidnappers in vans are abducting children for prostitution and illegal organ trades.

sections.label: Rumours inciting mob violence
sections.summary: Rumours and fake news that she threw items at a mosque and disrupted prayers incited mobs to burn and ransack Buddhist temples, causing billions of rupiahs in damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Rumour has it, then fake news, that she also threw items at the mosque and disrupted prayer sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This incited angry mobs who started burning and ransacking Buddhist temples with damages running into billions of rupiahs.

sections.label: Executive action and SC Recommendation 12
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Executive branch acting and cites SC Recommendation 12 that POFMA measures must break virality within hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, I believe and I support that the Executive branch, supported by the Civil Service, should be the right party to act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I also want to point out that in the SC report, there was a Recommendation 12, and I have an excerpt here, and I quote, "New legislation", talking about POFMA, "will need to be implemented to combat online falsehoods and such legislation should have the following objectives." And prime among them, No 1, I quote, "the measures will need to achieve the objective of breaking virality by being effective in a matter of hours." I am quoting the SC report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I would also want to point out that Mr Pritam Singh is a member of the SC, and the Committee collectively agreed that whatever law is legislated and whoever is the decision-maker, it is very, very important that actions must be able to be taken in a matter of hours.

sections.label: Pritam Singh and Executive option
sections.summary: The speaker says Pritam Singh agreed to Recommendation 12 and supported the Executive option, and quotes Assoc Prof Goh on the judicial process being too slow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As a Member and the WP Leader in the SC, he agreed to Recommendation 12, that whichever party is to be made the decision-maker, that party must be able to act in a matter of hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: He is a learned man, in the School of Law and he supported the Executive option, which means that the Minister, supported by the Civil Service, will be the party making such decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And here again, I want to quote what the report said: "Assoc Prof Goh explained that the judicial process, while important, may not be sufficiently fast to deal with the rapid spread of online falsehoods.

sections.label: POFMA and fake news
sections.summary: The passage states that Courts are empowered as final arbiters of truth while POFMA empowers Ministers and the Civil Service, and stresses the practical need to act quickly against fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, the Court may require a hearing before coming to any decision." So, there are eminent and learned persons who support the Executive being the decision-maker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: But to be fair, there were also some representors at the SC who were sceptical of the Executive action, but they, too, and I quote from the report: "also accepted that there are situations, such as those involving public order, national security and workings of public institutions where only the Executive...", and these are the sceptics who were representing to the SC, "where only the Executive will hold the facts and where the facts should be backed by the authority of the Executive." Here, I assume the whole machinery of the Civil Service supporting the Executive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While POFMA is to empower Ministers and the Civil Service to act, of course, the Court is empowered as a final arbiter of truth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the court of public opinion will be the final judge of whether the Government has done its job well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, I am less excited about the idealism or the imagined complexity, or some may say, the falsehood around the POFMA Bill, than the practical need for us to act quickly against a very real present and very critical problem – fake news.

sections.label: Speedy court remedies for falsehoods
sections.summary: The passage discusses using Harassment Courts for quick remedies against online falsehoods, citing a Minister's example of companies losing billions in hours and a fake news case about seniors' transport top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I will deal with the second issue first because that is more pertinent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We found out during the POHA debate yesterday that when there is an issue affecting an individual or a company, there is an easy form to fill out – or at least this is what the Minister assured us – for individuals or companies to take action to deal with online falsehoods quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And we know that there was a reference made to making that process more straightforward, streamlined, easier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I used an example during the POHA debate about a matter that was brought up by Minister Shanmugam on 13 April in a Channel NewsAsia interview where he said that you can have a situation of a company, an online falsehood has been made against it, and in four or five hours, billions of dollars could be lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: If individuals are expected to rely on the Harassment Courts for quick remedies, it is my position that we can expect a speedy response to come from the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: That I can concede, that you will need Courts to respond quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But it does not contradict my signing off from the SC Report on an option to ensure that the response is a speedy one because I believe that the Courts can respond speedily and that the expedited timeline or an appropriate interim order can deal with the prima facie falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Questions of having to sieve through evidence really turn on how real the issue is, and the prima facie nature of the evidentiary threshold should deal with the issue of speed.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, there was this fake news that seniors can get a $30 transport top-up if they go to the community centres (CCs) before 12 November.

sections.label: CPF inheritance fake news
sections.summary: The passage states that some people spread fake news claiming that after people died, their CPF cannot be passed on to inheritors in cash form.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some people also spread fake news that after people died, their Central Provident Fund (CPF) cannot be passed on to their inheritors in cash form.

sections.label: France anti-minority fake news
sections.summary: The passage states that in France, accounts from foreign countries have been spreading anti-minority fake news, resulting in increased inter-racial violence.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recently, in France, accounts from foreign countries have been spreading anti-minority fake news, resulting in the increase of inter-racial violence.

sections.label: EZ-Link top-up hoax
sections.summary: The passage states that last year a hoax claimed all senior citizens would get a free $30 top-up on their EZ-Link cards at the CCs on 12 November.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, there was a hoax which claimed that all senior citizens would get a free top-up of $30 on their EZ-Link cards at the CCs on 12 November.

sections.label: Halal food hoaxes
sections.summary: The passage states that many hoaxes claim halal-certified food is actually haram, spreading panic in the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Already, we see many hoaxes saying that halal-certified food is actually haram, spreading panic in the Muslim community.

sections.label: Low Thia Khiang on Government power
sections.summary: Mr Low Thia Khiang claims the Bill gives absolute power, but the Minister said it contains narrower powers increasing Court oversight.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Low Thia Khiang claims that the Bill gives the Government absolute power.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He completely overlooks and fails to address what the Minister said yesterday that the Bill contains a narrower set of powers which increase oversight for the Courts.

sections.label: Court challenge to false statements
sections.summary: People can quickly bring a challenge to Court, and the Court decides whether there is a false statement of fact.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People can easily and quickly bring a challenge to Court and the Court will decide on whether there is a false statement of fact.

sections.label: Low's examples called clear opinions
sections.summary: Mr Low's examples are clear opinions, and the Minister for Law clarified this in his speech and circulated examples.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Low Thia Khiang also suggests that the Bill may be used against comments, for example, saying that the Pioneer and Merdeka Generation Packages are to buy votes.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These examples Mr Low cited are all clear opinions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister for Law clarified this yesterday, both in his speech and through the list of examples he circulated.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Low should not mislead when the position in the Bill is clear.

sections.label: Speedy response through Judiciary
sections.summary: Some responses must be dealt with within hours, and a speedy response can be foreseen through the Judiciary as decision-maker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Obviously, there will be instances where the response has to be dealt with within hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The SC report does not commit to the Executive as the decision-maker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And I think the point that needs to be re-emphasised is that there is no need for me to take my name away from any conclusion of the SC report, I stand by it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But a speedy response can be foreseen, can be fathomable through another decision-maker, namely, the Judiciary.

sections.label: Quick process and separate Courts
sections.summary: During the POHA Second Reading, it was said that applying against online falsehoods would be quick, with separate Courts set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Yesterday, during the POHA Second Reading, we were informed that the process of applying against online falsehoods for individuals and companies would be a quick one and separate Courts have been set up for this for Singaporeans, for individuals and for companies.

sections.label: POFMA about public interest
sections.summary: POFMA is about public interest, riots, possible spread of wild fire, and racial disharmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: POFMA that we are debating now is about public interest, it is about riots, it is about possible spread of wild fire, it is about racial disharmony.

sections.label: Recommendation 12 Government powers
sections.summary: Recommendation 12 says the Government should have powers to disrupt online falsehoods, with legislation breaking virality within hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Singh, Recommendation 12 opens with "The Government should have the powers to swiftly disrupt the spread and influence of online falsehoods" – "The Government".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And then, it goes to set out these capabilities should be able to apply to all relevant platforms; and it goes on to say, "Legislation will be needed to achieve the above objectives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Such legislation should have the following objectives: measures will need to achieve the objective of breaking virality by being effective in a matter of hours." On the face of it, the recommendation is that the Government should have these powers.

sections.label: POHA process and timelines
sections.summary: Under POHA, dedicated Courts are set up, with private interest cases hoped to be done in two days or a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In POHA, the process is as follows: we have set up dedicated Courts but we have not pretended that in POHA it can come within a matter of hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But private interest, in general, we think they can go and try, but we hope that it can be done in two days; in sufficiently suitable cases, hopefully a day sometimes.

sections.label: No guaranteed Court timing
sections.summary: Anyone claiming a Court will always decide within hours when needed is not telling the truth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If anyone in this House says that you guarantee that a Court will decide every single time, within a matter of hours, when you need it, you are not telling the truth.

sections.label: Removing Executive as decision-maker
sections.summary: The decision to remove the Executive as the decision-maker was made clear in the original draft.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I do not intend to read from them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But very clearly, my decision to remove the Executive as the decision-maker was made quite clear in the original draft.

sections.label: POFMA advantage to Government
sections.summary: A tech company would be expected to challenge the Government, but POFMA gives advantage to the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Yes, I would agree that if we came to a tech company I would expect them to challenge what the Government wants to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But in that sort of situation, the fact is POFMA gives advantage to the Government.

sections.label: Interim order prima facie standard
sections.summary: Under POHA, for an individual or company, an interim order requires meeting the prima facie standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And then, it goes on to say a statement, a specified statement and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We look at the identical option under POHA, for individual or company, there is a requisite standard to meet for an interim order, which is the prima facie standard.

sections.label: Interim order service and dispensation
sections.summary: Clause 16 states an interim order takes effect when served on the respondent, or when the Court dispenses with service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Clause 16 says: "an interim order takes effect in respect of the respondent", and this is an individual or company, "when the order is served on the respondent in such a manner as may be prescribed", but critically, (b) says, "where the Court dispenses with the service of the order, when the service of the order or the respondent is dispensed with by the Court, or at such a later time as the Court may specify".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Again, it suggests to me that the regime can be dealt with to deal with the problem of a falsehood provided that prima facie threshold is met.

sections.label: Duty judge for urgent cases
sections.summary: A duty judge regularly hears urgent cases rather than one judge waiting only for Government applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is not as if there is one judge sitting there, doing nothing else but waiting for the Government to come in and apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is a duty judge regularly to hear urgent cases.

sections.label: Interim order before service
sections.summary: Provisions in urgent matters allow an interim order to be obtained before service.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Okay, let us say we make provisions in urgent matters, we can come and get an interim order in the first place even before service.

sections.label: Breaking virality after order
sections.summary: After getting the order, virality is broken within hours rather than by an immediate Ministerial order.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Even then, after you get the order, you are going to break the virality within a matter of hours, as supposed to an immediate order by the Minister?

sections.label: Court capacity for POFMA cases
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Courts could be resourced, restructured, or given new processes and judges for urgent POFMA interim decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Is it the position of the Law Minister and the Government that our Courts could not be sufficiently resourced, structured, if necessary a new process, a new expedited process created, if necessary a new process for assigning judges created, additional capacity created?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Is it inconceivable that this could be done in the future in order to issue interim prima facie decisions in urgent, time-sensitive cases under POFMA?

sections.label: Stopping communication within two hours
sections.summary: The passage asks whether going to Court could stop a communication within the next two hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He has to go to finish the case for the sitting, until lunch time or until the evening, depending on the scenario.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we are saying, if supposing something has happened and I want to stop the communication within the next two hours, do you think it is possible by going to Court?

sections.label: Court urgency and due process
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether urgent court decisions can definitionally always be dealt with in hours, given due process.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if he does that, and the other side turns up, and then they say, "We do not have time to file an affidavit but we want to know the basic facts before we can argue.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We need until this evening; we need until tomorrow morning." Once you set up a Court process, then, you must allow for the due process.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, my point to you, Mr Leon Perera is, having now heard this explanation, is it your position that definitionally, it is possible, every single time, whenever we want it to be dealt with urgently, that it can be dealt with urgently, in a matter of hours?

sections.label: Courts breaking virality quickly
sections.summary: The speaker asks if courts can always decide within hours to break virality, and answers yes if structured and resourced.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When I said "not agree", it may be because he says, "I want to hear what the other side has got to say".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, my point to Mr Perera is: therefore, we can take it, and it will be very simple, can I take it your position is that, definitionally, every single time it is necessary to make a decision, you believe that the Courts can be used to make a decision to break the virality within a matter of hours; every single time, when it is necessary to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: If the Courts are sufficiently structured and resourced and the process is defined to enable that to happen, then the answer is yes.

sections.label: Simplified process to minimise lead time
sections.summary: The Member proposes a simplified process to minimise the lead time between the Minister and the Court for a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What I am saying to the hon Minister is that a simplified process can be created to absolutely minimise the lead time between the Minister and the Court to get a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: There is a certain amount of lead time, in any case, for the internal conversation between civil servants and Ministers in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What we are talking about is the additional lead time between the Minister and the Court to get that decision to break the virality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, I would put it to the Minister that a process can be defined that is very simplified to minimise that lead time.

sections.label: POFMA section 22 falsehoods
sections.summary: Section 22 of POFMA defines falsehoods as false or misleading statements, so a Minister can deem a misleading statement false by omission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: As the hon Member Mr Pritam Singh said, section 22 of POFMA defines falsehoods as statements of facts that are false or misleading, not false and misleading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, a misleading statement can be deemed false by a Minister by virtue of omission of facts.

sections.label: POFMA harmful falsehoods and public interest
sections.summary: A misleading collection of facts can be deemed grave, and section 4's public interest criteria lack a real risk threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: On POFMA, a falsehood can be deemed grave enough to warrant correction or penalty for being a misleading collection of facts, even if it does not contain one single false statement of fact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Next, section 4 sets out various criteria by which false statements are deemed harmful to the "public interest".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: However, the language lacks any reference to a real risk threshold.

sections.label: Section 4F harmful falsehoods
sections.summary: Section 4F defines harmful falsehoods as including those that diminish confidence in the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Two, section 4F defining harmful falsehoods as including those that diminish confidence in the Government.

sections.label: POFMA burden of proof
sections.summary: Under POFMA, the burden of proof falls on the person making a statement, not on the Government saying it was false.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Under POFMA, the burden of proof falls on the person saying something, not the Government for saying that something was false.

sections.label: Missing public interest defence
sections.summary: The POFMA Bill lacks a public interest defence, which the UK is reportedly considering for its fake news law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The POFMA Bill, as it stands, lacks a public interest defence, something the UK is reportedly considering including in its eventual fake news law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: There should be a public interest defence whereby a statement that was "false", according to the strict standards of POFMA, that is, it could have been deemed misleading at the time that it was made, may still not be an offence, or would be a far smaller class of offence carrying smaller penalties if made in good faith using a defensible process and to serve the greater public interest.

sections.label: Diminution of confidence in Government
sections.summary: Section 4F defines diminution of confidence in the Government as a harmful falsehood, differing from most similar foreign laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Section 4F describes diminution of confidence in the Government as one definition for falsehood being harmful to the public interest, a feature of this law that is different from most similar fake news laws or draft laws in other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Is vesting powers this broad in the Government of the day, from now to when this law is repealed, if ever that day comes, the responsible thing to do for future generations of Singaporeans?

sections.label: POFMA and electoral accountability
sections.summary: A rogue government could use POFMA powers to stop voters learning negative information and partly insulate against electoral accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: A number of PAP Members of this House have made a great deal of this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But Mr Speaker, Sir, this ignores the fact that a rogue government can precisely use POFMA powers to stop voters from learning negative information about their actions which could be a factor in those very elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The powers can be used to partly insulate against electoral accountability.

sections.label: WP requests for fake news law
sections.summary: The WP requests that the Government prove falsehoods, Courts arbitrate first, and Ministers not receive dangerous powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The WP requests for a fake news law that places the responsibility of proving falsehoods on the Government, and not the person who issued the statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The Courts must be the first arbiter in making the decision, and the Ministers should not be given dangerous powers, such as those stated in this Bill, powers that can be misused by an irresponsible government to retain their power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, Sir, purging destructive falsehoods from the public square is the right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But this Bill is a cure worse than the disease.

sections.label: Foreign fake news laws
sections.summary: Germany enacted the Network Enforcement Act, France passed the Law Against the Manipulation of Information, and the UK is consulting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Germany had enacted the Network Enforcement Act which took effect this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: France passed the Law Against the Manipulation of Information last November.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The UK is now holding an open public consultation on the Online Harms White Paper that sets out the government’s plans for measures to keep users safe online.

sections.label: Seniors and online dangers
sections.summary: Older people may be less familiar with technology and online dangers, and the Government has introduced programmes such as Silver InfoComm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Unlike the young, they may be less familiar with technology and the dangers that are lurking in the online space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government has introduced some programmes and initiatives, such as the Silver InfoComm.

sections.label: Consulting stakeholders on obligations
sections.summary: It asks whether stakeholders will be consulted on how the obligations should be framed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will stakeholders be consulted on how the obligations should be framed?

sections.label: Bank runs and financial contagion
sections.summary: A post crashed Ethereum's price, and bank runs can make even healthy banks insolvent and cripple a financial ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The post led to a crash in the price of Ethereum and US$4 billion was wiped out in just five hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: During the Financial Crisis in 2007 to 2008, there were rumours that the Bank of East Asia was in financial trouble, leading to thousands of panicked depositors queuing outside the bank's branches to withdraw their savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Regardless of the actual financial health of a bank, in the event of a bank run, when a large number of customers withdraw their deposits simultaneously, even a healthy bank could become insolvent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In turn, its collapse could potentially lead to other bank runs, and, like a fast-spreading virus, soon cripple an entire financial ecosystem.

sections.label: Delay, online falsehoods and class actions
sections.summary: The speaker opposes measures hampering quick Ministerial action on online falsehoods, suggests class action suits, and asks about mistaken use of powers affecting markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Any delay may ultimately cause severe harm to ordinary Singaporeans, some of whom may see their life savings wiped out in a matter of hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I do not support measures which will hamper the ability of our Ministers to react quickly to clamp down on online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Enormous damage, some of which may be irreversible, would have occurred over those precious hours and days of delay – damage which the perpetrators do not have to be responsible for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The onus should be on the parties making claims online to present the facts and evidence to support their assertions instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I think we should consider allowing class action suits brought against service providers by the victims themselves harmed by tech companies which fail to rectify or take down fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While falsehoods by malicious actors can have a serious impact on the financial markets, is it possible that a mistaken exercise of the powers under this Bill may also have a serious impact on the financial markets?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share how the Government will mitigate the risk of making such mistakes?

sections.label: Minister's decision can be challenged
sections.summary: The Minister's decision can still be challenged by anyone going to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: I know the WP's argument is that you would prefer the Court to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: But do not forget, the Minister's decision still can be challenged; anyone can still go to Court and challenge.

sections.label: Minister decides falsehood, Court appeal
sections.summary: Under the Bill the Minister decides what is falsehood and what action to take, and affected parties can appeal to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the Minister decides what is falsehood and what action to take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: If the affected party disagrees, he can go to Court to appeal and let the Court decide.

sections.label: Compliance with Minister's order
sections.summary: The Bill requires compliance with the Minister's order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: According to this Bill, you must comply with the Minister's order.

sections.label: Obey Minister then Court
sections.summary: One must first obey the Minister's order and then go to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: You must first obey the Minister’s order, then go to Court.

sections.label: Support for POFMA Bill
sections.summary: The speaker calls the Bill timely and important, understands the need for POFMA, and supports it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is a timely and important Bill that has garnered much interest and debate both in and outside of this Chamber.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand the need for the POFMA Bill and, in essence, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Media and information literacy initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker supports media and information literacy initiatives such as NLB's SURE Programme, IMDA's Silver Infocomm Junctions and MCI's framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The need for our people and for our young to be media and information literate is all the more important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I support current initiatives to do so, such as NLB's SURE (Source, Understand, Research, Evaluate) Programme, the IMDA's Silver Infocomm Junctions and the National Information and Media Literacy Framework by MCI.

sections.label: Definition and value of academic freedom
sections.summary: The speaker quotes a definition of academic freedom and says academics value it for research, questions, data, opinions and critique.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If I may loosely quote the definition of "academic freedom" from Brittanica: "Academic freedom, is the freedom of teachers and students to teach, study and pursue knowledge and research, and without unreasonable interference or restriction from current laws, institutional regulations or public pressure." Academic freedom is highly valued by academics because it allows us to carry out our research work, ask questions, collect relevant data, write and share our opinions, and critique freely and openly, without fear or favour.

sections.label: POFMA, academic freedom and integrity
sections.summary: The speaker asks how far POFMA allows academic freedom and argues academic freedom cannot exist without academic integrity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To what extent will POFMA allow academic freedom to continue to exist?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having argued for academic freedom, I must also put forth the following argument, that academic freedom cannot exist without academic integrity.

sections.label: Academic freedom assurance and advisory panel
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to assure academics of continued academic freedom and suggests an Academic and Research Advisory Panel to review disputed work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many academics that I know are not worried about the curtailment of academic freedom from this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We are confident that as long as you practise academic integrity and are able to support our academic or research arguments with data, we will still have academic freedom to carry on our academic research work and still publish our work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, in light of the above arguments, may I seek the Minister’s assurance, for the record, that academics and researchers can continue to enjoy academic freedom as long as they demonstrate academic integrity in our work or publications, and that we will not always need to make appeals for our work that may discuss data or information that may run counter or even dispute facts or data owned or shared by Government Ministries or agencies?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, may I suggest that an Academic and Research Advisory Panel be set up to review academic or research work or publications that may be deemed to publish "false statements of facts"?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The purpose of the Academic and Research Advisory Panel is to have oversight and decide on academic or research work or publications that would otherwise need to be put up as appeals to the Courts.

sections.label: Ministers as truth gatekeepers
sections.summary: An objection is that the Bill gives Ministers and their alternate authorities, as interested persons, the job of gatekeeping truths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One such key objection is that the Bill entrusts the job of gatekeeping truths to Ministers and their alternate authorities who are part of the executive Government and would be making certain decisions as interested persons rather than neutral arbiters.

sections.label: Mobile phone users and the Bill
sections.summary: Anyone who uses a mobile phone can fall afoul of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Anyone who uses a mobile phone can fall afoul of the Bill.

sections.label: High Court appeal grounds and burden
sections.summary: Clause 17(5) lets the High Court set aside a Part 3 Direction only on three grounds, with individuals bearing the burden of proving truth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clause 17(5), for example, it is provided that the High Court "may only set aside a Part 3 Direction on any of the following grounds on an appeal: (a) that the person did not communicate in Singapore the subject statement; (b) that the subject statement is not a statement or is a true statement of fact; or (c) that it is not technically possible to comply with the direction".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The burden of proof falls to the individuals to prove that his statement was true.

sections.label: Limited judicial oversight of Ministers
sections.summary: The assessment is that judicial oversight of Ministers' powers under POFMA is severely limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Looking into the totality then, it is my assessment that the powers of judicial oversight of Ministers' powers under POFMA are severely limited.

sections.label: Economists rebuked over job figures
sections.summary: Two economists were rebuked for job figures the Government refuted with statistics showing nine of ten new jobs went to residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Two economists were rebuked by the Government for putting up job figures suggesting that the majority of new jobs were taken up by foreigners in the previous five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This was strongly refuted by the Government which then released statistics previously not disclosed showing that, in fact, for every 10 jobs created, nine went to residents.

sections.label: Correction Directions and innocent falsehoods
sections.summary: The Bill targets all statements the Government deems false, and Correction Directions may be issued even if the communicator did not know the statement was false.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill is not only targeted at deliberate falsehoods, but at all statements the Government deems false, even if innocently communicated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clauses 11(4) and 12(4), it is stated that Correction Directions may be issued by the Minister or the alternate authority even if the person who communicated the statement did not know or had no reason to believe that the statement is false.

sections.label: POFMA lopsided and ministerial power
sections.summary: POFMA is lopsided and gives Ministers too much power in matters where they may be interested parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: POFMA is lopsided and gives the Ministers too much power in matters where they may be interested parties.

sections.label: Minister's role and correction
sections.summary: In most cases the Minister informs the public of a falsehood and issues correction Directions, while the original post can be retained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In most cases, the Minister's role is to inform the public that a falsehood has been put out and to issue Directions for correction, while the original post can be retained.

sections.label: Court as first arbiter
sections.summary: If the Court is the first arbiter, it is akin to using water far away to put out a fire nearby.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If the Court is the first arbiter, then it is akin to using water far away to put out a fire nearby.

sections.label: Punishment as execution
sections.summary: As to whether the punishment can be considered an execution, the answer is yes, it is an execution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: As to whether the punishment can be considered as an "execution", my answer is "yes, it is an execution".

sections.label: Appeal after correction order
sections.summary: Lodging a court appeal after being ordered by the Minister to clarify on the website is like complaining to the Courts after being executed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: If you lodge an appeal with the Courts after being ordered by the Minister to clarify on the website, it is like complaining to the Courts after you have been executed.

sections.label: Government authority to shut websites
sections.summary: The Government has authority under existing legislation to shut down websites including Facebook, which would cost the Prime Minister 1.2 million followers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: With regard to the question of timing, based on existing legislation, the Government has the authority to shut down websites, including Facebook, but that would mean the Prime Minister would lose 1.2 million followers.

sections.label: Bill gives public access to corrections
sections.summary: The Bill's key feature is giving the public access to corrections so they can compare original and correction, addressing market failure from fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To me, the most important feature of the Bill is its ability to give the public access and visibility to the corrections, because then the public decides, comparing the original and the correction, on what is to be believed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Countries around the world have either implemented some form of legislation or are exploring it to tackle fake news, not only because of the risks of falsehoods and its spread, but also because tech and new media companies that are used as platforms to viral these fake news are either incapable of or unwilling to solve the entirety of the problem, leading to market failure in the form of a negative externality.

sections.label: Indonesians believed fake news
sections.summary: 25% of Indonesians polled and 42% of Prabowo supporters believed the news about Jokowi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As many as 25% of Indonesians polled believed this news and as many as 42% of the Prabowo supporters believed this about Jokowi.

sections.label: False claim about Cebu priest
sections.summary: In the Roman-Catholic Philippines, a false claim about a Cebu-based parish priest was consumed by over 185,000 people and triggered anti-Catholic comments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In majority Roman-Catholic Philippines, false claims that a Cebu-based Parish priest had impregnated two daughters of his associate priest was consumed by more than 185,000 people and triggered anti-Catholic comments from other religious quarters.

sections.label: Bill enforces Correction Direction remedy
sections.summary: The Bill allows Government agencies to engage credible views and enforces a remedy, likely a Correction Direction, for false statements against public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, it will allow Government agencies the bandwidth and precision with which it can engage credible views thereby strengthening political discourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, even when there is a statement of fact that is false, and it is against public interest, the Bill will enforce a remedy that will most likely be a Correction Direction – to carry a clarification while the false statement can remain up.

sections.label: Indonesian election political fake news
sections.summary: Mafindo documented political fake news using ethnicity and religion in Indonesia's election, with a 61% surge and fake articles targeting Jokowi and Prabowo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: During the recent Indonesian Presidential Election, the country's fact-checking agency, Mafindo, documented political fake news that used ethnicity and religion to target both Presidential candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Its report showed that political fake news experienced a 61% surge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: President Jokowi fell victim to 75 fake news articles that went viral, while his challenger, Prabowo, experienced 50 such incidents.

sections.label: Facebook group attacks Shia followers
sections.summary: A Facebook group called Singapore Malays Reject Shiism has 1,814 members who often attack Shia followers, and Mr Hazrul Jamari said he encountered beheading videos spread through social media in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The social media group in Facebook called Singapore Malays Reject Shiism has 1,814 members who are often found attacking the Shia followers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Hazrul Jamari, who gave evidence at the SC hearings, said that he encountered videos of beheadings in Syria that had been spread through social media in Singapore.

sections.label: Bill and religious history claims
sections.summary: Claims about history and interpretation of religious history would not be included in the Bill, but falsehoods used to create tension can be countered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How would this Bill deal with such incidents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It must be clarified that claims related to history and the interpretation of religious history would not be included in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, if falsehoods have been used to create tension, this Bill can help to counter it.

sections.label: False statement against public interest
sections.summary: The law will only be used if a statement of fact is false and against public interest, likely resulting in a correction Direction placed alongside the false statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The law will only be used if a statement of fact is false and goes against public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If such a case happens, it is likely that the measure taken will be a correction Direction, that is, to place the correction alongside the false statement.

sections.label: Court as final arbiter
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam said the Court will be the final arbiter if a party seeks review of a Minister's decision, with the case heard in as early as nine days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If any party feels that a Minister's decision needs to be reviewed, Minister Shanmugam has said earlier that the Court will be the final arbiter, and the case will be heard in as early as nine days.

sections.label: Correcting Zaqy Mohamad's quote claim
sections.summary: In Malay, the speaker corrects Mr Zaqy Mohamad's claim that he played with quotes, saying the late Prime Minister's words can be interpreted to include Government bodies, statutory bodies and the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, I would like to correct what was said by Mr Zaqy Mohamad when he stated that I was playing with the quotes that I mentioned, which were words spoken by the late Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I said that the words uttered by the late Prime Minister can be interpreted this way, that the Government includes Government bodies, statutory bodies and also the Civil Service and vice-versa.

sections.label: Appeal and judicial review tracks
sections.summary: An appeal to the Supreme Court concerns the truth or falsity of the representation and its attribution to a person in Singapore, alongside a separate judicial review of the Minister's decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: An appeal to the Supreme Court on the issue of the truth or falsity of the representation and attribution of the representation to a person in Singapore as well as a parallel track of a judicial review of the Minister's decision, which operates separately.

sections.label: Appeal process and timelines
sections.summary: The passage states there is an appeal process with timelines for it to complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, there is an appeal process and there are timelines for the appeal process to complete.

sections.label: Minister states Direction reasons
sections.summary: The speaker's concern was assuaged because the Minister said reasons are stated when a Direction is issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But having reviewed the material closer, my concern on this matter has been assuaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is because I noted that the Minister stated yesterday, at the point when a Direction is issued, the Minister would have to nail his or her colours to the mast by stating the reasons why the Direction is being issued.

sections.label: Executive burden and POFMA conditions
sections.summary: The legal burden rests with the Executive to prove Part 3 Directions meet the falsity and public interest criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The legal burden has always rested with the Executive to prove that the Part 3 Directions comply with the criteria for "falsehood" as well as "public interest".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed POFMA, there are two cumulative conditions: falsity of the statement of fact and public interest.

sections.label: Streamlined procedure for fast action
sections.summary: The procedure was streamlined so the Executive can act fast without losing accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And that is why we cannot afford to have inaction or slow action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And that is why the procedure has been streamlined to allow for the Executive to take action fast but without losing the accountability that the regime contemplates.

sections.label: Commenting on Correction order
sections.summary: The passage states a person can comment on the Correction order and on the Ministerial action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Most times, we are talking about a Correction order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He or she can comment on the correction order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He or she can comment on the Ministerial action.

sections.label: Reading of misleading in section 2(2B)
sections.summary: The speaker reads "misleading" in section 2(2B) as focusing on statements weaving truth with fiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The way I read section 2(2B) is that the intention behind the usage of "misleading" is to focus on statements of fact that weave truth with fiction, such that it creates a distorted statement which is false.

sections.label: Court as POFMA safeguard
sections.summary: The Court, through judicial review, acts as referee and safeguard against a Minister issuing a Direction for political aims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In that kind of situation, it is pretty clear to me, reading POFMA, that it would not be consistent with the definition of public interest for a Minister to issue a Direction to further his or her political aims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The safeguard is the Court because the Court, through judicial review, would be the referee.

sections.label: Conflicted Minister cannot decide
sections.summary: A Minister who is conflicted cannot make that decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If a Minister is conflicted, he cannot make that decision.

sections.label: Concern over parallel judicial procedures
sections.summary: Two parallel procedures providing for judicial oversight may in certain circumstances create difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And I believe this is the point that the hon Member Mr Vikram Nair made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I have a concern that two parallel procedures providing for judicial oversight may, in certain circumstances, create difficulties.

sections.label: Concerns on judicial review risks
sections.summary: Concerns are raised about use of a Supreme Court Judge's resources and risk of inconsistent decisions between High Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is not necessarily the most judicious use of a Supreme Court Judge's resource.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am also concerned that there could be a risk of inconsistent decisions as a High Court decision on the truth of the representation is not necessarily binding on the High Court dealing with the judicial review.

sections.label: Suggestion for statutory review procedure
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it considered a statutory review procedure with appeal so a person can challenge falsity and public interest in one shot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, it can be, for example, open to the High Court to decide the statement is true because Hindi is offered in our schools and, therefore, it is a recognised language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, to guard against these possibilities, I wonder if the Ministry had considered enacting a statutory review procedure, together with the appeal procedure, such that a person who wishes to challenge the Minister's decision on falsity and public interest, can do it in one shot.

sections.label: Retaining judicial review, same judge
sections.summary: There is merit in retaining judicial review on public interest, with the same High Court Judge deciding both matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, I think there is merit in retaining judicial review in relation to exercise of public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The same High Court Judge should decide on both matters.

sections.label: Judicial review leave procedure
sections.summary: A leave procedure can be stipulated to sift out unmeritorious judicial review applications, and statutory review procedures should be simplified and cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To guard against abuse of process of judicial review, there can even be a stipulation for a leave procedure to sift out unmeritorious applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is important that statutory review procedures be simplified and be rendered cost-effective.

sections.label: Legal burden in appeals
sections.summary: The legal burden in appeal proceedings arises only if there are legal proceedings, meaning an appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The first point he made was in relation to the legal burden in any appeal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And it goes without saying, and I agree fully with him, the legal burden would only arise if there are legal proceedings, meaning if there was an appeal.

sections.label: Judicial resource for POFMA appeals
sections.summary: The second point concerns sufficient judicial resource, and the Government elevated a POFMA appeal on representation of fact to the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In relation to the second point, I believe the second point concerns about making sure that there is sufficient judicial resource.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And, in fact, it occurred to me that the Government obviously is taking POFMA issues seriously because it could have designated an appeal from a POFMA issue relating to a representation of fact at the District Court level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: What it did here is to elevate it to the Supreme Court level.

sections.label: Candidates for Supreme Court appointments
sections.summary: Despite progress in the Bar, no more than 10 people can be offered as candidates for Supreme Court judicial appointments because the process is rigorous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In fact, we have made a lot of progress in our Bar, but I cannot think of more than 10 people whom I can offer as candidates for judicial appointments in the Supreme Court because it is a very rigorous process.

sections.label: POFMA and chilling effect
sections.summary: If POFMA focuses only on false statements of fact rather than opinion, the chilling effect issue can be examined to see if it is perceived or real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: If we accept for the moment that all that POFMA is focused on is not opinion but statements of facts which are false, then the issue about chilling effect can be viewed a little bit more carefully and see whether, indeed, it is really perceived or real.

sections.label: POFMA Bill penalties and orders
sections.summary: The POFMA Bill allows jail up to 10 years and fines up to $100,000 for individuals and $1 million for legal persons, with Ministers issuing correction or removal orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   	According to the POFMA Bill, individuals who disseminate falsehoods that undermine the public interest can be jailed up to 10 years, fined up to $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Legal persons can be fined up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Bill, the Government can issue mandatory orders to individuals and online platforms to correct or remove falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Every Minister has the power to decide which information is genuine or false or against the public interest, and issue directives to correct or remove the information, even if the information has been amended or is no longer being disseminated in Singapore.

sections.label: Court appeal against Minister directives
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Court set aside Minister's directives in three circumstances, including when the statement is not a falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for that appeal, the Bill stipulates that the Court can only set aside the Minister's directives under three circumstances: if "the person did not communicate in Singapore the subject statement; it is not technically possible to comply with the Direction"; or if "the subject statement is not a statement of fact, or is a true statement of fact" – in other words, the information is not a falsehood.

sections.label: Sri Lanka social media ban
sections.summary: Other countries lacking these tools resorted to disproportionate measures, such as Sri Lanka banning social media sites after the Easter Sunday bombings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In some other countries, the lack of these tools has led the government to resort to disproportionate measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We saw this in Sri Lanka, where in the immediate aftermath of the Easter Sunday bombings, the Sri Lankan government moved to ban various social media sites, including Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram among others, to pre-empt divisive misinformation.

sections.label: SC recommendation on online falsehoods
sections.summary: The SC's key recommendation was to disrupt online falsehoods by breaking the virality of fake news and increasing the reach of corrections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The key recommendation by the SC was to disrupt online falsehoods by breaking the virality of the fake news and increase the reach of corrections.

sections.label: Speed of putting up correction
sections.summary: The passage asks how fast a correction must be put up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How fast must a correction be put up?

sections.label: Unwitting sharing not an offence
sections.summary: The Minister has said more than once that the Bill does not make it an offence for a person who unwittingly shares an online falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Minister has mentioned on more than one occasion that the Bill does not make it an offence for a person who unwittingly shares an online falsehood.

sections.label: Minister corrects WP misconceptions
sections.summary: The Minister corrected misconceptions that the Court is final arbiter, the Bill covers only facts, and it targets falsehoods affecting public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Even in this debate, we have heard from Members of the WP that the Bill will have a chilling effect on free speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, glad that the Minister has corrected these misconceptions: one, that the Court will be the final arbiter of what is to be considered true or false; two, that the Bill only pertains to statement of facts, not opinions, not criticism nor satire; and three, that the Bill is targeted at falsehoods that affect public interest.

sections.label: New tools against online falsehoods
sections.summary: The Bill gives new tools and measures for swift Government action against deliberate online falsehoods and manipulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What is new is the advent of technologies that help to spread such fake news at a rate faster than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This Bill, therefore, provides us with new tools, new measures to fight against deliberate online falsehoods and manipulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government must be able to take swift action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Ministers with the domain expertise must be able to be in a position to speedily conclude whether a statement of fact is false and what course of action is in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nothing stops the original author nor the platform nor anyone else from commenting on the original post or the evidence provided by the Minister, or the Correction Direction itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If Ministers cannot intervene early, in a calibrated manner, falsehoods can quickly erupt into violence, as we have seen in many other countries, which will then warrant more drastic measures for us to take.

sections.label: Academics signing letter on 6 May
sections.summary: As of 6 May afternoon, the letter was signed by 124 academics, of whom 71 are foreign and 52 Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of the afternoon of 6 May, as reported by Assoc Prof Walter Theseira earlier on, the letter was signed by 124 academics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
